solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Probe inside garment, one being worn with one gun hidden

parts.note: inside means in
a vest is a garment worn under a shirt

indicators.note: with something hidden, other letters are tucked out of sight within this pair

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
clothes being worn are on
gat is old slang for a gun
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone frisks a suspect whose vest conceals a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' tucks the gun and the second one inside the pair formed by 'one being worn'; the charade pieces are joined in answer order, not the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough inquiry, the same thing as an official investigation.

clue.text: Requests may be terribly insensitive putting two couples off initially

indicators.note: terribly signals that the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
two couples are four letters, and putting them off initially strips the first four from the word

explanation.surface: An invitation might come across as tactless when it excludes two pairs of guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting two couples off initially' removes INSE, the first four letters of INSENSITIVE, leaving NSITIVE; 'terribly' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: Invites, used informally as a noun, are requests for someone's company.

clue.text: Naughty lad is under vehicle — first sign of mischief noted here?

definitions.text: Naughty lad is under vehicle — first sign of mischief noted here?

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies under comes after

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: naughty signals that the letters misbehave and get rearranged
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bad boy hides beneath a van, and graffiti on it shows his mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges LAD IS into DALIS, placed under VAN in the down light; M comes from 'first sign of mischief'. The whole clue also pictures a vandal at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalism is wilful damage to property, the kind of mischief a naughty boy might do to a parked van.

clue.text: Fish was off, we may deduce?

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs a piece of fish and concludes it has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on what one infers from fish that has gone off: it gave off a bad odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small silvery food fish; a thing that was off gave off a bad odour, so it stank.

clue.text: Get in Uri for bending — underhand scheme?

indicators.note: bending, as a spoon-bender bends cutlery, means the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Bring in Uri Geller to bend spoons, a cunning plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller is the showman famous for bending spoons, which makes 'bending' a natural anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigue is secret plotting, a crafty scheme carried on behind someone's back.

clue.text: Feature of a religious group — keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the group's letters enclose another piece

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A trait of a silent monastic order is its vow of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a facet or characteristic, a particular part of something.

clue.text: Jew is having a religious ceremony in which aged Liberal participates

indicators.note: an element that participates in a ceremony is inside it, so these letters go within the rite

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony
ae. is the abbreviation for aged, as on memorials

explanation.surface: A Jewish man takes part in a religious service attended by an elderly Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which ... participates' puts AE (the abbreviation of Latin aetatis, aged) and L inside RITE, giving RAELITE after IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite is a member of the ancient Hebrew people, a biblical term for a Jew.

clue.text: Lord showing no bitterness, one having been ousted

indicators.note: something ousted is thrown out, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: bile figuratively means bitterness or bad temper
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A peer bears no grudge after being expelled from office.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is an aristocrat, a member of the peerage like any lord.

clue.text: Minister's short account about the end of government

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the extra letter
short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a record is an account of events

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A government minister's abbreviated report concerns the fall of the administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts RECORD to RECOR, and 'about' wraps it round T, the end of 'government'. The 's is a link: Minister is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a clergyman in charge of a parish, a minister of the Church.

clue.text: Wine and a bit of bread for the French boy

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
bread is slang for money, and a cent is a small bit of it

explanation.surface: A French lad is given wine and some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so 'a bit of bread' is a coin, not a crumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent is a common boy's name in France.

clue.text: Butler featuring in feeble story

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: pale can mean feeble or weak, as in a pale imitation
Rab Butler was a senior British Conservative politician of the mid-20th century

explanation.surface: A manservant appears in a weak tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant but is R. A. 'Rab' Butler, a British Conservative statesman who served as Chancellor and Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral story, such as those told in the Gospels.

clue.text: Publication that covers a lot of ground?

definitions.text: that covers a lot of ground?

explanation.surface: A pamphlet that ranges widely over its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as a wide-ranging text, but means a large stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political, and also an extensive area of land.

clue.text: A bit more severe after change of direction

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, a change of direction, so R becomes L in the word

parts.note: an increment is a small added amount

explanation.surface: Something gets slightly harsher once it turns a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) is replaced by L (left), the 'change of direction'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement describes harsh or stormy weather, so it means severe.

clue.text: Prolongs explanation for using fast bowlers only?

definitions.text: explanation for using fast bowlers only?

explanation.surface: A cricket captain drags things out by relying on pace alone.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowlers are either fast or spin; a side using only pace bowlers has left spin out, read as SPIN'S OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out a task is to make it last longer; read as spin's out, it says slow spin bowling is excluded.

clue.text: To get out of the way at speed is dodgy

definitions.text: To get out of the way

indicators.note: dodgy, meaning unreliable or crooked, signals that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting out of someone's path at high speed is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: To step aside is to move out of someone's path, or to withdraw from a post.

clue.text: German children may be more helpful

explanation.surface: Youngsters in Germany may be nicer to have around.
explanation.walkthrough: Kinder is German for children, as in kindergarten.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinder is the German word for children; it is also the comparative of an adjective meaning considerate or generous.

clue.text: Audacious action going wrong in strange uprising

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another
in a down light, an uprising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: odd means strange
erring means going wrong or making a mistake

explanation.surface: A bold deed goes awry in a peculiar revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' means reading upward in a down light, so the word for strange is turned before 'in' sets the other piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring, heroic action, the stuff of swashbuckling adventure.

clue.text: Monster in little boys' room that's troubled many after start of evening?

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the one before

parts.note: the little boys' room is a jokey name for the toilet, and bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A child fears a monster lurking in the toilet that scared many at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a lavatory. 'troubled' rearranges the clue word many, and 'after' places the result following the first letter of evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an imaginary monster used to frighten children.

clue.text: Spoil voting sheet with 100 X's written in!

indicators.note: written in means added inside, so a letter goes within the sheet

parts.note: a ballot paper is a voting sheet
X is ten in Roman numerals, so a hundred of them make a thousand, which is M

explanation.surface: Ruin a ballot by marking it with a hundred crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: '100 X's' is arithmetic: 100 times 10 is 1,000, Roman M. The surface suggests a spoilt ballot paper, though spoil here means indulge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to indulge someone excessively, which is to spoil them.

clue.text: The old man and the old woman embracing a new country

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the parents' letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, so pa
the old woman is slang for mother, so ma

explanation.surface: An elderly couple welcome a newcomer to their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' places AN after the P of PAMA: P-AN-AMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American nation on the isthmus between the two Americas.

clue.text: Shabby attire journalist has on at party

indicators.note: on at says the following pieces are placed on, after, the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
gear means clothing or attire
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter turns up at a party in scruffy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared describes pages with turned-down corners, hence worn and tatty.

clue.text: Fault makes one resign without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the word for resign goes round the other piece

parts.note: demit is an old word meaning to resign from office
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A blunder forces someone to quit at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; demit is a rare old verb for resigning an office. 'makes one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone, a fault or failing.

clue.text: Polish off Friday fare eating at home

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the food encloses another piece

parts.note: fish is traditionally eaten on Fridays, when many Christians avoid meat
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone clears their plate of the Friday fish supper at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off a meal is to eat it all up, to complete it.

clue.text: Fruit from tree in can after processing

indicators.note: processing, as food is processed, means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit from an orchard is canned after it has been processed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Excommunication of priest admitting foremost of sins

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the priest's letters take in another piece

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchman is cast out for confessing his worst transgression.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE is the French curé, a parish priest; accents are ignored in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse in church law is an anathema, a formal exclusion from the community of the faithful.

clue.text: Theatrical Miss is a solid figure

explanation.surface: An actress is described as a stout, well-built lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Prism is the governess in Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Prism is a stage character in Wilde's comedy; in geometry a prism is a three-dimensional shape with matching ends.

clue.text: Trees with needles beginning to fall

explanation.surface: Conifers start to drop their needles.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the verb: one who pines wastes away, starting to go into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Pines are evergreen conifers bearing needle-like leaves; to pine is to languish or waste away, a decline setting in.

clue.text: Saint helping beggar with half a cloak and one drink

parts.words: Saint helping beggar with half a cloak
parts.note: St Martin of Tours famously cut his cloak in half to share it with a freezing beggar
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A kind saint shares his cloak with a beggar and gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend of St Martin of Tours: as a soldier he sliced his cloak in two and gave half to a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Mum, one who scolds half-heartedly and who tries to cope?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle pair of letters, and half-heartedly loses one of them

parts.note: a nagger is a person who scolds

explanation.surface: A mother who nags only halfway is someone trying to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of NAGGER is GG; 'half-heartedly' drops one G, leaving NAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is someone who handles things, getting by under pressure.

clue.text: Plant has unusual spot on the leaf

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A plant has an odd blemish on its leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant's foot is a succulent with a swollen, wrinkled base resembling a large animal's limb.
